title: Shed, don't cap: a 429-driven preemption supervisor with a requeue ledger instead of static concurrency knobs
idea: Flip to 100 concurrent agents against real rate limits: static admission caps are the wrong shape because the limit is a moving external signal, not a known constant — which is plausibly why /optimize deliberately removed its max_concurrent knob rather than tuning it. Kernel: govern reactively. Every fan-out tags spawns with a shed-priority; a lightweight supervisor watches for 429/limit signals and, on pressure, kills the lowest-priority in-flight agents and writes them to a requeue ledger for serial replay after backoff, so a rate-limit storm degrades to slower instead of '6 of 7 agents failed'. VERIFY_N_CAP stays as the panel-size sanity bound it was born as; this adds the runtime layer that caps structurally cannot provide. The intake's cap-of-3 becomes just the most conservative shed-priority profile rather than a hand-enforced rule in workflow scripts.

title: Route around the rate limit: 429 pressure sheds offloadable work to the $0/external provider lane instead of queueing it
idea: T13's fifty-three ideas all treat 429s as a throttling problem — backoff (T13-F1-3), AIMD (T13-F5-3), requeue (H-F6-6), leases (T13-F1-4). T2's fifty-two ideas treat providers as a cost problem — Ollama as $0 offload, DeepSeek as cheap second opinion. Nobody wrote the intersection: external providers do not consume the Anthropic rate budget, so under sustained 429 pressure the correct move for offload-class units (mechanical, non-gated, chaperone-verifiable per {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch}) is not to wait — it is to reroute to the registry's local/external lane, expanding effective concurrency at zero marginal Anthropic tokens. Concretely: the shared backoff wrapper (T13-F4-3's primitive) gains a reroute branch that consults engine_resolver for an eligible offload row when a unit is tagged offloadable, HALTing (not degrading) for gated/judgment units, and stamping the reroute in the dispatch ledger. This converts the 6-of-7-agents-killed failure mode into partial forward progress.

First-principles: rate limits are per-provider; the fleet already has a registry seam (engine_resolver.py/engine_registry.py, intake §5) designed to route work by intent, so capacity relief is a new routing *reason*, not new machinery. Constraint compliance: only offload-intent, never-gatekeepers-safe units reroute; Claude remains verifier-of-record; judgment units still queue — this stays inside {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} rather than revisiting it.
outcome_shape: PR extending the shared 429-retry primitive with a registry-consulting reroute branch for offload-tagged units + dispatch-ledger reroute stamps; test simulating 429 storms asserting offload units reroute, gated units HALT-queue, and every reroute is ledgered.
